css.description: The CSS tooltip is enabled by adding a data-uc-tooltip attribute to an element. It is suitable for short, static supplementary content.

elements.name: data-uc-tooltip
elements.description: The text displayed by the tooltip on hover, focus-visible, or focus-within.

elements.name: Trigger content
elements.description: The tooltip is rendered with a CSS pseudo-element, so the attribute value is text content rather than React content.

hook.description: useTooltip returns event handlers and aria-describedby props for an interactive trigger. The shared TooltipLayer renders and positions the active tooltip.

elements.name: content
elements.description: The tooltip content. It accepts any React node. The tooltip is disabled when the content is null, undefined, false, or an empty string.

elements.name: placement
elements.description: The position relative to the anchor: top, bottom (default), left, right, top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right, left-top, left-bottom, right-top, or right-bottom.

elements.name: delay
elements.description: The opening delay in milliseconds. Defaults to 0. Keyboard focus opens immediately.

elements.name: positionRef
elements.description: An optional ref to the HTMLElement used as the positioning anchor instead of the event target.

elements.name: Returned props
elements.description: Spread the returned props onto the trigger. They include pointer/focus handlers and aria-describedby.

elements.name: mergeTooltipProps
elements.description: Merges existing element handlers and attributes with the props returned by useTooltip without replacing either set of handlers.

accessibility.general: The hook associates the trigger with a shared element using aria-describedby and renders that element with role="tooltip". Tooltips are supplementary and should not be the only way to provide essential information.
elements: Keep tooltip content short and supplemental. Put essential instructions, errors, or action names in the trigger's accessible name or surrounding content.
Use a visible label or an explicit aria-label for icon-only triggers; the tooltip does not replace the trigger's accessible name.
The hook ignores touch pointer entry, opens on visible keyboard focus, and closes on blur, pointer leave, or Escape.
The CSS attribute does not create an ARIA relationship automatically, so provide an accessible name independently when needed.
